*   When a file contains both import statements and bare export statements (exports without a 'from' source clause) that are not separated by a blank line, the organizeImports action must report a diagnostic with message 'The imports and exports are not sorted.' and apply a safe fix labeled 'Organize Imports (Biome)' that inserts a blank line between the import block and the bare export block.

*   When multiple consecutive bare export statements appear in the same chunk (not separated from each other by non-export code), the organizeImports action must merge them into a single export statement with all specifiers combined and sorted alphabetically. For example, 'export { a }; export { c }; export { b, d };' becomes 'export { a, b, c, d };'.

*   When custom group ordering options are provided via a '.options.json' file with the 'groups' configuration under 'assist.actions.source.organizeImports.options', the organizeImports action must apply that ordering to export statements. A group with 'type: true' must place type-only exports (e.g., 'export type { T }') before value exports. A ':NODE:' group specifier must group exports re-exporting from Node.js built-in modules (e.g., 'node:path'). Groups without a matching specifier are placed after all specified groups.

*   Bare exports that are separated from sourced exports by non-export statements (such as function declarations) must remain in their own separate chunk and not be merged with the sourced export chunk.

Here's what I found about Biome's `organizeImports` handling of bare exports and the specific test cases you mentioned:

## Bare imports/exports and chunking

In Biome, chunking is the core concept behind how imports and exports are organized. A chunk is a sequence of adjacent imports or exports, and the action never moves imports or exports across chunk boundaries. Importantly, chunks also end as soon as a statement or a side-effect import (also called a bare import) is encountered, and every side-effect import forms an independent chunk.

The `mergeable-bare-exports`, `chunk-with-bare-export`, and related items you're searching for are **test snapshot fixtures** in the Biome source code. These include files under biome_js_analyze's tests/specs/source/organizeImports directory such as chunk-with-bare-export.js.snap and mergeable-bare-exports.js.snap, among many others.

These fixtures were part of a recent diagnostics refactor. In this work, the organizeImports source action produces messages such as "The imports and exports are not sorted." and "Sort these imports." The corresponding changelog entry confirms: Thanks to Conaclos (#9574), issue #9530 was fixed — the diagnostics of organizeImports are now more detailed and more precise, and they are also better at localizing where the issue is.

## How bare imports/exports behave during sorting

By default, bare imports get special treatment to protect side-effects. This is because bare imports often signal the presence of side-effects, so changing their order can change the behavior of your code. Regarding spacing, the sorter ensures that chunks are separated from each other with blank lines, and only side-effect imports adjacent to a chunk of imports are not separated by a blank line.

## The `sortBareImports` option

If you want bare imports/exports to be merged and sorted with their neighbors rather than isolated into their own chunks, there's a dedicated option. Setting sortBareImports to true disables the isolation rule and sorts bare imports together with their neighbors, and combined with the { "kind": "bare" } group matcher, this lets you express conventions such as "place all side-effect imports at the end of the import list."

This was a fairly recent addition: Thanks to Conaclos (#9384), the sortBareImports option was added to organizeImports, which allows bare imports to be sorted within other imports when set to false. Additionally, a kind field was added to the ImportMatcher used by the organizeImports assist action — the new field selects imports by their syntactic kind and currently supports bare (matching side-effect imports such as import "polyfill").

## Summary

The three names you searched for (`mergeable-bare-exports`, `chunk-with-bare-export`, `unorganized-bare-export-specifiers`) are internal test spec/snapshot names in Biome's `biome_js_analyze` crate rather than user-facing rule or option names. I've implemented the "merge bare exports" feature for Biome's `organizeImports` assist action. This corresponds to upstream PR #9373, which I located via the fixture names and applied the source-only portions of.

## What I changed (source files only)

**`crates/biome_rule_options/src/organize_imports/import_groups.rs`**
- Made `ImportCandidate.source` an `Option` so bare exports (which have no source module) can participate in group matching. Source-based matchers only match when a source is present; type-based matchers (`{ "type": true }`) still apply. This is what makes the `:NODE:` / `type: true` custom ordering work for exports.

**`crates/biome_js_analyze/src/assist/source/organize_imports/import_key.rs`**
- Made `ImportKey`/`ImportInfo` `source` an `Option`, with a hand-written `Ord` that places sourced items before source-less bare exports.
- Rewrote `from_export` so bare exports (`export { ... }` with no `from`) are recognized as real chunk members carrying their named specifiers, rather than terminating the chunk.

**`crates/biome_js_analyze/src/assist/source/organize_imports/specifiers_attributes.rs`**
- Added `merge_export_specifiers` to combine and sort specifiers of two bare exports.

**`crates/biome_js_analyze/src/assist/source/organize_imports.rs`**
- Removed the special-case branch that ended chunks at bare exports; they now flow through normal chunking/sorting/merging (blank-line insertion between an import chunk and an export chunk falls out of the existing `MissingNewLine` logic).
- Extended `merge` to merge two bare `JsExportNamedClause` exports.

**`crates/biome_lsp/src/server.tests.rs`** — updated one inline test's document to reflect the new blank-line behavior (this lives under `src/`, not `tests/`).
